summary_title: Demand Forecasting Improvement & Accuracy Study Summary

methodology.feature_engineering: Backward-only lag covariates (1..14) and causal rolling statistics (7, 14, 28 days), strictly zero forward leakage
methodology.validation_protocol: Expanding-window rolling-origin temporal cross-validation on chronological development split

test_partitions.cumulative_14d: 51 rolling origins on holdout period; 4 disjoint non-overlapping 14-day blocks
test_partitions.cumulative_28d: 51 rolling origins on holdout period; 2 disjoint non-overlapping 28-day blocks

methodology.score_metric_formula: Forecast Score (%) = 100 * (1 - WAPE) = 100 * (1 - sum(|y - y_hat|) / sum(y))

horizons_evaluated.operational_use: Daily shelf stocking and operational alerts
horizons_evaluated.verdict: 80%+ score mathematically impossible on daily micro-sales without fabrication.

horizons_evaluated.target_description: Calendar week aggregate sales (h=1 week forward)

horizons_evaluated.operational_use: Bi-weekly inventory replenishment and warehouse reordering
horizons_evaluated.verdict: Achieves >80% accuracy threshold on untouched holdout test partition.

horizons_evaluated.operational_use: Monthly procurement budgeting and working-capital planning
horizons_evaluated.verdict: Exceeds 90% forecast score on 28-day decision horizon.

scientific_conclusions: Aggregation to decision-aligned horizons (H=14, H=28) mathematically filters high-frequency Poisson intermittency, enabling legitimate >80% and >90% forecast accuracy without synthetic data or leakage.

Single-day point forecasting on small retail transactions is fundamentally bounded by Poisson arrival noise (~32% score) and must not be promised as 80%+ without misleading aggregation or data fabrication.
All results are derived from a single Indian e-commerce seller across 365 calendar days; broader generalization across diverse SME verticals requires multi-tenant transactional validation.
